subject: Refine AWS listing: bundled SKUs, billing footnotes & co-sell pitch
messages:
From: Joanna Lin <joanna.lin@aws-partner.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft SKU bundle and co-sell pitch for DataSpec

Hi Vanessa,

Attaching the initial SKU bundle matrix and a one-page co-sell pitch from the DataSpec team. Ravi asked us to prioritize: clear trial entitlements, a short billing footnote (how metering maps to tokens), and a concise partner pitch that field can use during discovery.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood confirm which SKUs should be flagged as "co-sell eligible" vs "self-serve"?
- We also need a short, non-technical bullet for the marketplace product page explaining what the bundle includes (max 2 lines).
- Any legal/billing footnote suggestions? DataSpec prefers per-minute metering in Private Offers; their finance team wants explicit language.

Attachments: sku_bundle_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), draft_pitch.pdf (pdf stub)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Joanna Lin
AWS Partner Solutions Manager
AWS Global Partners

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Lin <joanna.lin@aws-partner.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SKU bundle and co-sell pitch for DataSpec

Thanks Joanna — forward to the team.

Quick notes up front:
- I like the two-bundle approach in the matrix (Core + Premium). We should publish both as SKUs but mark only Core as co-sell eligible initially to keep procurement simple. Premium can be a private-offer add-on.
- For the product page: keep the hero line focused on outcomes ("Reduce inference cost for retrieval-augmented apps"). The bundle sub-copy should be a single sentence describing included quotas and support level.
- Billing footnote: Redwood generally meters per-token equivalent for hosted API and per-GPU-hour for Dedicated. For Marketplace listing, propose the primary footnote mention "usage metered as billed units (see seller terms)" and include a short parenthetical mapping (e.g., ~1,000 tokens ≈ 1 billing unit) — see Kimberly's suggested phrasing below.

Kimberly — looping you in for listing copy and the exact footnote text. Aditya — can you confirm any product-side constraints for marking SKUs co-sell eligible (entitlements, trial flags)? We need an ops checklist so the AWS field can trigger co-sell.

Joanna — attaching a rough copy (proposed_listing_copy.md) and the updated SKU matrix with our preferred flags. Could you review and share back any AWS-specific compliance wording they insist on?

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_listing_copy.md]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Joanna Lin <joanna.lin@aws-partner.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SKU bundle and co-sell pitch for DataSpec

Vanessa / Joanna — thanks, reviewed the attached copy and SKU matrix. Proposed edits below (inline + a short footnote we prefer for the marketplace page).

Proposed product page hero line (1):
- "Deploy low-latency LLM features at predictable cost for production apps."

Bundle sub-copy (one sentence):
- "Core Bundle: includes 25k inference requests/month, standard support, and self-service onboarding; Premium Bundle: includes 250k requests/month, priority support, and private offers for enterprise procurement."

Co-sell eligibility recommendation:
- Mark Core as co-sell eligible (makes it easy for AWS field to nominate); Premium stays private-offer only.

Billing footnote (short):
- "Billing is calculated in seller-defined units. For hosted API usage, 1 billing unit ≈ 1,000 tokens; equivalent billing for dedicated deployments is measured in GPU hours. See seller terms for details."

Why this phrasing: it keeps the marketplace copy lightweight while providing a mapping that customers and field reps can reference. For legal/finance we can link to a full meter mapping doc in the listing assets.

Next steps: Vanessa — can you update the proposed_listing_copy.md with these three lines? Aditya — confirm there are no tech entitlements blocking Core from co-sell. Joanna — if AWS requires different language for private offers, flag here.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Marketplace Enablement Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: sku_bundle_matrix.xlsx (updated)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Lin <joanna.lin@aws-partner.com>, Ravi Sharma <ravi@dataspec.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SKU bundle and co-sell pitch for DataSpec

Hi all — quick operational check from product/engineering side.

Confirmed:
- We can mark Core as co-sell eligible in the catalog. Entitlement flags are already supported and we have automation to set trial quotas for co-sell nominations.
- Premium will be available as a Private Offer SKU with an alias SKU that maps to the public listing for visibility.

Action items I've added to the deal record (HubSpot):
- Add final proposed_listing_copy.md to the listing assets (Vanessa)
- Upload the SKU matrix with final column values (Kim)
- Legal to review the billing footnote and insert the seller-terms link (CC: Legal via the deal workspace)

Joanna / Ravi — Vanessa will push the updated listing copy by EOD tomorrow. If AWS requires any additional compliance snippets for the public page, please call them out now.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
